1	\chapter{The Jacobian datum}
     2	\label{chap:Jacobian}
     3	
     4	Throughout this chapter \(k\) is a field and \(C\) is the challenge curve: a
     5	scheme over \(k\), proper, smooth of relative dimension one, and geometrically
     6	irreducible. The degree-zero relative Picard functor
     7	\(\Pic^0_{C/k} : \Over(\Spec k)^{\op} \to \mathrm{CommGrp}\) was constructed in
     8	\ref{def:pic0Functor}. This chapter introduces the \emph{Jacobian datum} --- a
     9	representing object for \(\Pic^0_{C/k}\) together with the certificates its
    10	construction provides --- and develops what follows formally from it: the
    11	group structure and universal property of the representing object, its
    12	uniqueness up to canonical isomorphism, separatedness (every group scheme over
    13	a field is separated), the homogeneity supplied by translations, and, given a
    14	proper irreducible \emph{Abel source} mapping onto it, properness and geometric
    15	irreducibility.

    20	\begin{definition}[Jacobian datum]
    21	  \label{def:jacobian_data}
    22	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData}
    23	  \uses{def:pic0Functor}
    24	  \leanok
    25	  A \emph{Jacobian datum} for \(C\) consists of:
    26	  \begin{enumerate}
    27	    \item a scheme \(J\) over \(k\);
    28	    \item a representation of the degree-zero relative Picard functor by
    29	      \(J\): a family of bijections
    30	      \(\Hom_{\Over(\Spec k)}(T, J) \cong \mathrm{pic}^0(C, T)\), natural in
    31	      the test object \(T\);
    32	    \item the certificate that the structure morphism of \(J\) is locally of
    33	      finite type;
    34	    \item the certificate that the structure morphism of \(J\) is
    35	      quasi-compact.
    36	  \end{enumerate}
    37	  The two certificates come from the construction of the representing object
    38	  and are carried as part of the datum rather than re-derived.
    39	\end{definition}
    40	
    41	\begin{definition}[The group structure of the representing object]
    42	  \label{def:jacobian_data_grp}
    43	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.grpObj}
    44	  \uses{def:jacobian_data, def:pic0Functor}
    45	  \leanok
    46	  For a Jacobian datum \(d\) with representing object \(J\), the scheme \(J\)
    47	  is a group object of \(\Over(\Spec k)\), with multiplication, unit and
    48	  inversion induced by the commutative-group structure of
    49	  \(\mathrm{pic}^0(C, -)\) through the representation.
    50	\end{definition}
    51	\begin{proof}
    52	  \leanok
    53	  Transport the group structure across the natural bijections of
    54	  \ref{def:jacobian_data}: each \(\Hom(T, J)\) becomes a group, naturally in
    55	  \(T\) --- precomposition with any \(T' \to T\) is a group homomorphism
    56	  because the restriction maps of \(\Pic^0_{C/k}\) are. By the Yoneda lemma the
    57	  natural transformation
    58	  \(\Hom(-, J) \times \Hom(-, J) \to \Hom(-, J)\) given by the pointwise
    59	  products is induced by a unique morphism \(\mu : J \otimes J \to J\), and
    60	  similarly for the unit \(1 \to J\) and the inversion \(J \to J\); the group
    61	  axioms hold for these morphisms because they hold pointwise on
    62	  \(T\)-points.
    63	\end{proof}

    65	\begin{lemma}[The universal property, consumer form]
    66	  \label{lem:jacobian_data_homEquiv}
    67	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.homEquiv,
    68	    AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.homEquiv_comp}
    69	  \uses{def:jacobian_data, def:pic0Functor}
    70	  \leanok
    71	  Let \(d\) be a Jacobian datum with representing object \(J\). For every test
    72	  object \(T\) there is a bijection
    73	  \[
    74	    \theta_T : \Hom_{\Over(\Spec k)}(T, J) \;\cong\; \mathrm{pic}^0(C, T),
    75	  \]
    76	  natural against restriction: for \(f : T' \to T\) and \(g : T \to J\),
    77	  \[
    78	    \theta_{T'}(g \circ f) \;=\; f^*\bigl(\theta_T(g)\bigr),
    79	  \]
    80	  where \(f^*\) is the restriction map of \(\Pic^0_{C/k}\)
    81	  (\ref{def:pic0Functor}).
    82	\end{lemma}
    83	\begin{proof}
    84	  \leanok
    85	  This is the representation carried by the datum (\ref{def:jacobian_data}),
    86	  with its naturality read element-wise.
    87	\end{proof}

    89	\begin{definition}[Uniqueness of the representing object up to canonical
    90	    isomorphism]
    91	  \label{def:jacobian_data_unique}
    92	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.uniqueUpToIso,
    93	    AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.homEquiv_uniqueUpToIso_hom}
    94	  \uses{def:jacobian_data, lem:jacobian_data_homEquiv}
    95	  \leanok
    96	  Let \(d\), \(d'\) be two Jacobian data for the same curve, with representing
    97	  objects \(J\), \(J'\) and universal bijections \(\theta\), \(\theta'\). There
    98	  is a canonical isomorphism \(\sigma : J \cong J'\) in \(\Over(\Spec k)\),
    99	  characterised by the intertwining property
   100	  \[
   101	    \theta'_T\bigl(\sigma \circ f\bigr) = \theta_T(f)
   102	    \qquad \text{for every } f : T \to J .
   103	  \]
   104	\end{definition}
   105	\begin{proof}
   106	  \leanok
   107	  Let \(u = \theta_J(\mathrm{id}_J) \in \mathrm{pic}^0(C, J)\) be the universal
   108	  class of \(d\), and set \(\sigma = \theta'^{-1}_J(u) : J \to J'\).
   109	  For \(f : T \to J\), naturality of \(\theta'\)
   110	  (\ref{lem:jacobian_data_homEquiv}) gives
   111	  \[
   112	    \theta'_T(\sigma \circ f) = f^*\bigl(\theta'_J(\sigma)\bigr)
   113	    = f^*(u) = f^*\bigl(\theta_J(\mathrm{id}_J)\bigr)
   114	    = \theta_T(\mathrm{id}_J \circ f) = \theta_T(f).
   115	  \]
   116	  Symmetrically there is \(\sigma' = \theta^{-1}_{J'}(u') : J' \to J\), where
   117	  \(u' = \theta'_{J'}(\mathrm{id}_{J'})\), with
   118	  \(\theta_T(\sigma' \circ f') = \theta'_T(f')\) for every \(f' : T \to J'\).
   119	  The two composites are identities: e.g.\
   120	  \(\theta_J(\sigma' \circ \sigma) = \theta'_J(\sigma) = u =
   121	  \theta_J(\mathrm{id}_J)\), and \(\theta_J\) is injective, so
   122	  \(\sigma' \circ \sigma = \mathrm{id}_J\); likewise the other composite.
   123	  Uniqueness of an isomorphism with the intertwining property follows from
   124	  injectivity of \(\theta'\) at \(T = J\).
   125	\end{proof}

   241	  Let \(G\) be a group object in a cartesian monoidal category, with unit
   242	  \(e : 1 \to G\) and difference morphism
   243	  \(\delta = \mathrm{pr}_1 \cdot \mathrm{pr}_2^{-1} : G \otimes G \to G\)
   244	  (\ref{def:grp_diff}). Then the square
   245	  \[
   246	    \begin{array}{ccc}
   247	      G & \xrightarrow{\ \Delta = \langle \mathrm{id}, \mathrm{id}\rangle\ }
   248	        & G \otimes G \\
   249	      \downarrow & & \downarrow \delta \\
   250	      1 & \xrightarrow{\ e\ } & G
   251	    \end{array}

   260	  \circ \Delta)^{-1} = \mathrm{id} \cdot \mathrm{id}^{-1} = 1\), the constant
